title: Degradation Inspector: signal fusion + fuzzy alert matcher for noisy SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Degradation Inspector service that fuses traces, metrics, and logs into a single degradation score per route/model and applies a fuzzy alert matcher to reduce noisy / duplicate pages. This ticket covers: adding lightweight tracing hooks to capture head/tail latency histograms, enriching metric streams with trace-derived attributes, piping selected logs into an anomaly detector, and extending the alerting engine to support a fuzzy matching deduplication layer and adaptive paging windows. Goal is to reduce actionable pager noise by ~40% while preserving burn-rate sensitivity for true SLO violations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Degradation score produced and ingested into SLO pipeline for >= 80% of routes in prod canary region. 2) Fuzzy alert matcher groups related signals (traces/metrics/log spikes) and suppresses duplicate pages in 95% of synthetic incident runs. 3) Burn-rate alerts still trigger within configured window with <10% regression on detection latency compared to baseline. 4) Dashboards for latency/error attribution show trace linkbacks and the top 5 contributing spans for each degradation event.
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with Observability, Runtime, and Platform teams. Agreed on lightweight trace hook fields (route, request_hash, seq_len_bucket).
2025-02-24: PoC of degradation score implemented in notebooks using historical traces and p50/p95/p99 compaction. Initial PR created to add trace hook (GH: #1248).
2025-02-27: Metric enricher service prototype streams to testing cluster using sampling rate 1:200. Early results show high correlation between degradation score and SLO burn spikes.
2025-03-02: Fuzzy matcher algorithm shortlisted (cosine similarity on normalized signal vectors + time-window clustering). Running end-to-end canary in prod-like staging (cluster canary-obs-2).
decisions: Use sampled tracing hooks (1:100 default) to balance cost and signal fidelity — adjustable per-customer.
Compute degradation score at aggregator tier (near metrics ingestion) to reduce trace retrievals.
Adopt vectorized fuzzy matcher instead of rigid fingerprinting to better group multi-signal incidents across model variants.
Initial rollout limited to canary region and dedicated SLO routes (high-customer-impact routes) before broader expansion.
tradeoffs: Granularity vs cost: higher sampling improves root-cause precision but increases GPU/ingestion cost. Chosen default sampling rate reduces cost but may miss very short-lived spikes.
Matcher complexity vs explainability: vector similarity handles more cases but is less human-readable than strict rule-based dedupe; created dashboard views to surface top matching features.
Latency vs centralization: computing scores near ingestion reduces retrievals but increases coupling of metric pipeline; we add versioned APIs to mitigate rollout risk.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for trace hook schema and metric enrichment code. 2) End-to-end synthetic incident runs: inject latency in runtime canary service, verify degradation score rises and fuzzy matcher groups signals. 3) Chaos test: simulate dropped ingestion to ensure fallback to raw burn-rate alerts. 4) Load test: validate aggregator can handle peak of 10k updates/sec with <2s processing lag.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy trace hooks + degr-score aggregator to canary-obs-2 and enable fuzzy matcher in observation-only mode for two weeks. Stage 2 (selected routes): enable dedupe for high-impact customer routes with reduced sampling, monitor pages for 1 week. Stage 3 (global): enable for all routes with gradual sampling increase and optional per-tenant tuning.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression of pages could hide real incidents. Mitigation: fuzzy matcher defaults to monitoring mode; suppression requires manual opt-in per project and automatic escalation failsafe that reverts to burn-rate page after X missed detections.
Risk: Increased ingestion cost from trace enrichment. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and compensating batching at the aggregator tier.
Risk: Model drift for anomaly detector producing false positives. Mitigation: periodic retraining schedule and evaluation against labeled incidents dataset.
